title: The Truth Hour: After Dark
description: The late shift. Darnell calmly explains that the moon was decommissioned in 1974. Mildred always suspected as much.

lines.speaker: ronnie
lines.text: It's after dark on Snazzie FM, and the Truth Hour goes deeper. Our caller Darnell has been waiting patiently. Darnell, you're on the air.

lines.speaker: caller-darnell
lines.text: Evening, Ronnie. I'll keep this calm, because panic is exactly what they want. <p:0.4> The moon is not real.

lines.speaker: barry
lines.text: ...The moon.

lines.speaker: caller-darnell
lines.text: It's a projection, Barry. Has been since nineteen seventy four. The real one was decommissioned.

lines.speaker: ronnie
lines.text: Decommissioned. I always wondered.

lines.speaker: caller-darnell
lines.text: Maintenance costs, Ronnie. A real moon is very expensive to keep in orbit. So they switched to a hologram. Cheaper. Brighter.

lines.speaker: barry
lines.text: Darnell, the tides. The tides are caused by the moon.

lines.speaker: caller-darnell
lines.text: The tides are a subscription service, Barry. <p:0.4> They run the ocean on a schedule now.

lines.speaker: ronnie
lines.text: That would explain why they're so regular.

lines.speaker: caller-darnell
lines.text: Twice a day, Ronnie. Like clockwork. <p:0.3> Because it is, in fact, clockwork.

lines.speaker: barry
lines.text: Okay, Darnell, then what about eclipses? People predict those years ahead.

lines.speaker: caller-darnell
lines.text: Of course they can predict them, Barry. <p:0.3> It's a scheduled broadcast. They send out the calendar in advance. That's not science, that's programming.

lines.speaker: ronnie
lines.text: The moon has a release schedule.

lines.speaker: caller-darnell
lines.text: Two seasons a year, Ronnie. Full moons are the season finales.

lines.speaker: barry
lines.text: And the astronauts, Darnell? People walked on it.

lines.speaker: caller-darnell
lines.text: They walked on the previous model, Barry. <p:0.4> Before the upgrade. That footage is the last real moon we ever got.

lines.speaker: ronnie
lines.text: We had the moon, and we traded it in.

lines.speaker: caller-darnell
lines.text: Leased it back, Ronnie. We don't even own the moon anymore. We rent it.

lines.speaker: barry
lines.text: From who, Darnell? Who do we pay for the moon?

lines.speaker: caller-darnell
lines.text: You don't say the name out loud, Barry. <p:0.4> Not on a Tuesday.

lines.speaker: caller-mildred
lines.text: ...I knew it. <p:0.5> I KNEW IT, RONNIE.

lines.speaker: ronnie
lines.text: Mildred, welcome back. You're among friends.

lines.speaker: caller-mildred
lines.text: ...I haven't trusted the moon since my wedding. <p:0.4> It watched me. THE WHOLE TIME.

lines.speaker: barry
lines.text: The moon did not attend your wedding, Mildred.

lines.speaker: caller-mildred
lines.text: ...Then who paid for the band, Barry.

lines.speaker: ronnie
lines.text: She raises an excellent question.

lines.speaker: caller-mildred
lines.text: ...The buffet was free. <p:0.5> NOBODY ASKED WHY THE BUFFET WAS FREE.

lines.speaker: barry
lines.text: A free buffet is not evidence of a lunar conspiracy, Mildred.

lines.speaker: caller-darnell
lines.text: Follow the money, Barry. <p:0.3> It always leads back to the moon.

lines.speaker: barry
lines.text: It physically cannot lead back to the moon.

lines.speaker: caller-darnell
lines.text: That's what the moon pays people to say, Barry. <p:0.3> No offense. You're probably on the payroll and don't even know it.

lines.speaker: barry
lines.text: I am not on the moon's payroll.

lines.speaker: caller-mildred
lines.text: ...That's what a moon man would say, Barry.

lines.speaker: ronnie
lines.text: And on that, we'll take a break. Don't look up. <p:0.3> Or do. It's not real anyway.
